meaning.en: To take advantage of gaps in rules or in someone's attention to gain an advantage.
meaning.zh: 利用漏洞或机会谋取私利。

examples.zh: 有人专门钻法律的空子偷税。
examples.en: Some people exploit loopholes in the law to dodge taxes.

examples.zh: 你别想钻空子，规则对大家都一样。
examples.en: Don't try to find a loophole; the rules are the same for everyone.

usage.en: Verb-object, casual and derogatory; 空 is read kòng (a gap), and the object may be inserted (钻法律的空子).
usage.zh: 动宾短语，口语，贬义。“空”读 kòng，宾语可插入，如“钻法律的空子”。

meaning.en: An antique, or a person with old-fashioned ideas.
meaning.zh: 年代久远的古物，也比喻思想陈旧、守旧的人。

examples.zh: 爷爷收藏了不少老古董。
examples.en: Grandpa has collected a lot of antiques.

examples.zh: 他们都说我是个老古董，不会用智能手机。
examples.en: They all say I'm an old fogey who can't use a smartphone.

usage.en: Noun, casual; either literal antiques or, jokingly, an out-of-date person or thing.
usage.zh: 名词，口语，既指古董，也常用来戏称思想陈旧的人或过时的东西。

meaning.en: Petty calculations made for one's own advantage.
meaning.zh: 只为自己打算的精明算计。

examples.zh: 大家都有各自的小算盘，团队很难齐心。
examples.en: Everyone has their own agenda, so the team can hardly pull together.

examples.zh: 他心里打着小算盘，想独占功劳。
examples.en: He's making his own calculations, hoping to take all the credit.

usage.en: Noun, casual; usually 打小算盘 or 各打小算盘.
usage.zh: 名词，口语，常说“打小算盘”“各打各的小算盘”。

meaning.en: The trade or line of work one has done for years.
meaning.zh: 自己一向从事的职业。

examples.zh: 退休以后，他又干起了老本行。
examples.en: After retiring he went back to his old trade.

examples.zh: 做饭是我的老本行，你尽管放心。
examples.en: Cooking is my old line of work, so don't worry.

usage.en: Noun, casual; 行 is read háng (trade). Often 干老本行 or 重操旧业.
usage.zh: 名词，口语，“行”读 háng，常说“干老本行”。

meaning.en: The same old methods or arguments that have long been used and no longer work.
meaning.zh: 陈旧的一套方法、说法。

examples.zh: 你们还是老一套，一点新意也没有。
examples.en: You're still doing the same old thing, with nothing new.

examples.zh: 这种老一套的教学方法已经过时了。
examples.en: This old-fashioned way of teaching is outdated.

usage.en: Noun, casual and critical; often 还是老一套 or 老一套的….
usage.zh: 名词，口语，含批评，常说“还是老一套”“老一套的……”。

meaning.en: Narrow-minded, touchy and ready to bear grudges over trifles.
meaning.zh: 气量小，爱计较小事。

examples.zh: 他这个人小心眼，一句玩笑就记仇。
examples.en: He's petty and bears a grudge over one joke.

examples.zh: 你别这么小心眼，大家都是朋友。
examples.en: Don't be so petty; we are all friends.

usage.en: Adjective or noun, casual; also 小心眼儿 in the north. Can mean a petty person (他是个小心眼).
usage.zh: 形容词或名词，口语，北方也说“小心眼儿”。也可指气量小的人。

meaning.en: To secretly report someone's faults to a superior.
meaning.zh: 背地向上级或老师告发别人的过失。

examples.zh: 他常向老板打同事的小报告。
examples.en: He often tells tales to the boss about his colleagues.

examples.zh: 谁在背后打小报告，大家心里都有数。
examples.en: Everyone knows who has been snitching behind our backs.

usage.en: Verb-object, casual and derogatory; 向…打小报告.
usage.zh: 动宾短语，口语，贬义，常说“向……打小报告”。

meaning.en: A person who is made to take the blame for someone else's anger.
meaning.zh: 被别人用来发泄怒气的人。

examples.zh: 他在公司受了气，回家拿老婆当出气筒。
examples.en: He had a bad day at work and took it out on his wife at home.

examples.zh: 我可不是你的出气筒。
examples.en: I'm not your punching bag.

usage.en: Noun; 当出气筒 or 拿…当出气筒. Originally a pipe through which air escapes.
usage.zh: 名词，常说“当出气筒”“拿……当出气筒”。本指排出空气的管子。

meaning.en: To behave shamelessly and unreasonably in order to get one's way.
meaning.zh: 用不讲理、不要脸的手段达到目的。

examples.zh: 欠了钱还想耍无赖，没那么容易。
examples.en: Owing money and then playing the rogue won't be easy for him.

examples.zh: 她被孩子耍无赖的样子气笑了。
examples.en: The way the child was acting up shamelessly made her laugh in spite of herself.

usage.en: Verb-object, casual; 耍 means to play, in a pejorative sense. Often used when someone refuses to pay or admit fault.
usage.zh: 动宾短语，口语，“耍”带贬义，常指赖账、耍赖。

meaning.en: To eat or take things without paying.
meaning.zh: 白吃别人的东西，不付钱。

examples.zh: 他总爱到朋友家吃白食。
examples.en: He's always freeloading meals at his friends' houses.

examples.zh: 那家伙在饭馆里吃白食被抓住了。
examples.en: That guy was caught eating at the restaurant without paying.

usage.en: Verb-object, casual; for 吃白食 or 吃白饭. Also used loosely for living off other people.
usage.zh: 动宾短语，口语，也泛指不劳而获。

meaning.en: To use personal connections or improper means to get something done.
meaning.zh: 利用私人关系或不正当手段为人办事或谋取好处。

examples.zh: 他是靠开后门才进这家单位的。
examples.en: He got into this organisation by pulling strings.

examples.zh: 招生必须公平，不许给任何人开后门。
examples.en: Admissions must be fair, with no back-door deals for anyone.

usage.en: Verb-object, casual and derogatory; 走后门 is a close synonym and 开后门 means the one with power lets people in.
usage.zh: 动宾短语，口语，贬义。与“走后门”相近，“开后门”侧重有权者提供方便。

meaning.en: A person who works hard and uncomplainingly, asking nothing in return.
meaning.zh: 比喻勤勤恳恳、不计报酬、默默奉献的人。

examples.zh: 他像老黄牛一样为村子干了一辈子。
examples.en: He worked all his life for the village like an old ox.

examples.zh: 她是公司里默默无闻的老黄牛。
examples.en: She's the unsung workhorse of the company.

usage.en: Noun, positive; often 老黄牛精神 or 甘当老黄牛. The ox stands for patience and selfless labour.
usage.zh: 名词，褒义，常说“老黄牛精神”“甘当老黄牛”。牛象征任劳任怨。

meaning.en: Petty cleverness that wins small advantages but lacks real wisdom.
meaning.zh: 只顾眼前小利的、不顾大局的聪明。

examples.zh: 他爱耍小聪明，结果被人看穿了。
examples.en: He likes to be too clever by half and was seen through.

examples.zh: 做学问靠的是功夫，不是小聪明。
examples.en: Scholarship relies on hard work, not cheap cleverness.

usage.en: Noun, casual; usually with 耍/卖弄/要. Contrasts with 大智慧.
usage.zh: 名词，口语，常说“耍小聪明”“卖弄小聪明”。与“大智慧”相对。

meaning.en: To give permission or special help so that something can proceed smoothly.
meaning.zh: 给予许可或提供方便，让事情顺利进行。

examples.zh: 领导为这个项目开了绿灯。
examples.en: The leadership gave the project the green light.

examples.zh: 审批部门对重点企业开绿灯。
examples.en: The approval office clears the way for key companies.

usage.en: Verb-object, casual to neutral; 开绿灯 is the action, 绿灯 is the noun. Can also hint at favouritism.
usage.zh: 动宾短语，口语到中性。“开绿灯”是动作，“绿灯”是名词。有时暗含偏袒。

meaning.en: To make a laughing stock of oneself in public.
meaning.zh: 当众出丑，闹笑话。

examples.zh: 他在舞会上跳舞摔了一跤，出了个大洋相。
examples.en: He fell while dancing at the party and made a spectacle of himself.

examples.zh: 不会唱就别上台出洋相。
examples.en: Don't go up to sing if you can't and make a fool of yourself.

usage.en: Verb-object, casual; 出洋相 or 出大洋相. 洋相 meant the odd looks of foreigners, in the old treaty-port slang.
usage.zh: 动宾短语，口语。“洋相”原指旧时沿海口岸里对洋人行止的笑谈。

meaning.en: To deliberately pose a difficult problem for someone.
meaning.zh: 给别人出难办的问题，故意为难。

examples.zh: 老师给我们出了一道难题。
examples.en: The teacher set us a difficult problem.

examples.zh: 你别给我出难题，这事我真做不到。
examples.en: Don't put me on the spot; I really can't do it.

usage.en: Verb-object, casual; 给…出难题.
usage.zh: 动宾短语，口语，常说“给……出难题”。

meaning.en: To court someone's friendship in order to gain advantage.
meaning.zh: 为了谋取私利而与有权势的人套近乎。

examples.zh: 他到处拉关系，想谋个好职位。
examples.en: He's cultivating contacts everywhere for a good post.

examples.zh: 做生意不能光靠拉关系。
examples.en: Business can't depend on pulling strings alone.

usage.en: Verb-object, casual, mostly derogatory; the usual partner is 走门路 or 套近乎.
usage.zh: 动宾短语，口语，多含贬义，常与“走门路”“套近乎”并用。

meaning.en: To flirt improperly with a woman or touch her inappropriately; to take advantage of someone.
meaning.zh: 调戏、占便宜，尤指对女性。

examples.zh: 他在酒吧里想吃女孩子的豆腐，被拦住了。
examples.en: He tried to make a pass at a girl in the bar and was stopped.

examples.zh: 别吃我豆腐，我可不是随便的人。
examples.en: Don't take liberties with me.

usage.en: Verb-object, casual and derogatory; tofu is soft, so the picture is of something easy to push around.
usage.zh: 动宾短语，口语，贬义。豆腐软嫩，好欺负。

meaning.en: Jealousy at someone else's success; also literally conjunctivitis.
meaning.zh: 看见别人有名有利就嫉妒；也指结膜炎。

examples.zh: 看他升职了，有人就犯了红眼病。
examples.en: Seeing him get promoted, some people fell prey to the green-eyed monster.

examples.zh: 别得红眼病，大家都在努力。
examples.en: Don't get jealous; everyone is trying hard.

usage.en: Noun, casual; 犯/得红眼病. In English envy is green; in Chinese it makes one's eyes red.
usage.zh: 名词，口语，常说“犯红眼病”“得红眼病”。英语的嫉妒是绿色，汉语是红眼。

meaning.en: To try crafty tricks to deceive someone.
meaning.zh: 使用手段欺骗别人。

examples.zh: 你别跟我耍花招，我什么都看得出来。
examples.en: Don't play tricks on me; I can see through everything.

examples.zh: 他想耍花招赖账，没那么容易。
examples.en: He wants to dodge the debt by trickery, but it won't be easy.

usage.en: Verb-object, casual; also 玩花招 and 耍花样.
usage.zh: 动宾短语，口语，也说“玩花招”“耍花样”。

meaning.en: To cause trouble through carelessness.
meaning.zh: 惹出麻烦或闯祸。

examples.zh: 这孩子又捅了个大娄子。
examples.en: The child has caused another big mess.

examples.zh: 你可别给我捅娄子，要小心行事。
examples.en: Don't cause me any trouble; be careful.

usage.en: Verb-object, casual; 捅了个娄子 (caused a mess) is common. 娄子 is trouble, read lóu zi.
usage.zh: 动宾短语，口语，常说“捅了个娄子”，“娄子”指乱子。

meaning.en: To hinder someone's progress by getting in their way.
meaning.zh: 阻挠别人前进，从中牵制。

examples.zh: 她总是扯同事的后腿。
examples.en: She's always holding her colleagues back.

examples.zh: 大家一起使劲，别拖后腿。
examples.en: Let's all pull together and not drag the team back.

usage.en: Verb-object, casual and derogatory; 扯/拖/拉后腿 are interchangeable, the object may be inserted.
usage.zh: 动宾短语，口语，贬义。“扯/拖/拉后腿”通用，宾语可插入。

meaning.en: A stingy person who never gives anything away.
meaning.zh: 一毛不拔的吝啬鬼。

examples.zh: 他是个铁公鸡，从来不肯请客。
examples.en: He's a tightwad who never treats anyone.

examples.zh: 别指望铁公鸡捐款。
examples.en: Don't expect a miser to donate.

usage.en: Noun, casual; from the saying 铁公鸡，一毛不拔 (an iron rooster has no feathers to pluck).
usage.zh: 名词，口语，常与“一毛不拔”连用，铁公鸡没有毛可拔。

natural: be turned away at the door

meaning.en: To be refused entry or rebuffed by someone who isn't at home or won't see you.
meaning.zh: 被拒之门外，不被接待。

equivalents: be turned away at the door

examples.zh: 我去拜访他，却吃了闭门羹。
examples.en: I went to visit him and was turned away at the door.

examples.zh: 上门推销的人常常吃闭门羹。
examples.en: Door-to-door salesmen often get the door shut in their faces.

usage.en: Verb-object, casual; 吃了闭门羹. Said to be from a Tang-dynasty courtesan who refused visitors by serving them a bowl of soup.
usage.zh: 动宾短语，口语，常说“吃了闭门羹”。相传唐代一位名妓以羹拒客。

meaning.en: For a man to live off a woman's earnings instead of working himself.
meaning.zh: 男人依靠女人的钱生活。

examples.zh: 他整天吃软饭，一点上进心都没有。
examples.en: He lives off his wife all day, with no ambition.

examples.zh: 他不愿意吃软饭，宁愿自己打拼。
examples.en: He doesn't want to live off a woman and would rather make it on his own.

usage.en: Verb-object, casual and derogatory; the 'soft' food is said to be easy to swallow without effort.
usage.zh: 动宾短语，口语，贬义。“软饭”不费力就能吃。
